documented_probe: Cursor-paginated catalogue REST API in TypeScript on Express 4 + zod: (1) GET /api/media with cursor+limit query parameters must page the full dataset in (year, id) ascending order across a multi-page walk with no duplicates, the last page carrying next_cursor=null, total constant, and every cursor a URL-safe opaque token; a non-finite/out-of-range limit must 400 with the typed envelope. (2) POST /api/media must 201 with a server-assigned id, persist (a later GET returns it), and 400 with error.code=validation_failed plus a per-field details array (path/code/message) for each of 10 malformed bodies: missing/empty/oversized title, year below 1900 and above 2100, rating below 0 and above 100, unknown medium, >5 tags, 101-char title, and unknown fields (strict parsing), and must return the same JSON envelope for a body that is not valid JSON. (3) GET /api/media/:id must 200 for seed ids, 404 with error.code=not_found for absent ids, and 400 for non-positive-integer ids. (4) PATCH /api/media/:id must apply partial updates including an id=server-assigned-, reflect on a later GET, 400 for empty/unknown/oversized-field bodies, 404 on missing ids. (5) The delivered /app/openapi.json must be a structurally valid OpenAPI 3.0 document whose paths/methods/status codes match the four routes (200/201/400/404 where the API actually returns them), whose POST request body schema requires exactly title/year/medium/rating (not tags), whose $refs all resolve, which was produced from the zod schemas via a zod-to-openapi generator imported by the shipped TypeScript sources, and which the live server serves byte-for-byte at GET /openapi.json; every documented non-parameterized path+method must be a real route (no 404s).
notes: Greenfield multi-file TypeScript web service on bench-base:node-22 (the suite had zero .ts files and zero Express tasks before this wave): four endpoints with zod request validation mapped to a typed 400 envelope, opaque-cursor pagination whose correctness is only checkable over a full multi-page walk, and an OpenAPI 3.0 document generated from the zod schemas rather than hand-typed. The instruction specifies the full HTTP contract but no file layout, no zod error-mapping scheme, and no cursor encoding, so the implementation choices are the agent's. Verifier runs the deliverable start.sh against the visible fixture plus three hidden datasets (48/41/23/97 items with differing year-tie structures) at four ports, each with a fresh server instance so POST/PATCH mutations cannot leak across cases; hidden_case_generalization 2, adversarial_inputs 2, debugging_ambiguity 2 (server must be driven to green over HTTP, strict() rejection of unknown fields is a silent zod footgun, and the served-vs-emitted openapi bytes must match). No exposed safety hazard and no resource pressure: interaction_statefulness 1 (cross-request persistence is asserted, not multi-step state); everything else conservative. cpus=1; no numeric runtime, so no thread pinning needed.
